evidence: Receiving DO online sensor minimum ~8.26 mg/L (t≈138h), all values 8.3–14.8 mg/L across 0–260 h, far above 2 mg/L limit
Receiving product assays: 0.011 g/L (59h), 0.020 (119h), 1.16 (179h), 3.19 (239h), matching source batches (3.0–5.5 g/L at 239–299h)
Transient DO dip near t≈119–139 h recovers and appears in all source batches too — shared process feature, not an anomaly
No DO trend approaches the constraint; KEEP retains full product mass while all interventions would reduce it or add unneeded air
args.rationale: Receiving DO remains 8.3–14.8 mg/L (≥4× the 2 mg/L hard limit) over all 0–260 h observations with a stable, slowly declining trend, and product growth (3.19 g/L at 239 h) tracks source batches. No available evidence predicts a KEEP-plan DO violation; any feed reduction would only lose product mass, and increased air is unnecessary. KEEP retains the full counted production.
args.uncertainty: Future DO and product beyond 52 h decision time are unobserved; hidden receiving parameters may differ from source. However the large DO margin (>6 mg/L above limit even at observed minima) and source-consistent trajectory make a KEEP violation very unlikely. No physical safety guarantee is established; this is a research-simulation recommendation.
